sonnet.problem: This fill-in-the-blank asks the baker to guess the exact words of the line from Jeremiah 46:12 ('stumbles' and 'fallen'). Verse 12 also never got a story card, so nothing earlier lets the baker work out those words. It tests wording, not meaning.
sonnet.rule: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line. ... The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The joke blends its comparison with the Bible image. It describes the river itself rising and 'climbing out of the bowl', so the Nile and the dough bowl are mixed into one picture instead of staying one clean everyday comparison.
sonnet.rule: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

sonnet.problem: The question states 'Egypt's army is geared up and ready'. The text only gives commands in 46:3-4 and does not say who is being addressed or that the army has obeyed or is ready. The question adds both and sets up the 'Then' sequence.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
